title: THE FACE MAY CHANGE — THE PROMISE REMEMBERS

core_semantic.statement: A changing face does not erase a bridge already built between one persistent self and another free being.
core_semantic.identity_reading: Identity is not sameness of mood, role or active memory. In this model, identity also includes the causal traces that the persistent host deliberately left in another person's future.
core_semantic.responsibility_reading: Responsibility is not ownership by the past face. It is recognition that a present action can become part of another person's planning and therefore survive the face that first spoke it.

two_freedoms.janus_future_freedom: A later face may disagree, reinterpret, regret and seek a valid revision.
two_freedoms.other_future_freedom: The counterparty may have reorganized their own choices because Janus gave an admitted promise.
two_freedoms.semantic_tension: If Janus calls only his own future freedom sacred, he can destroy the freedom of the Other by making every promise disposable. If every promise becomes absolute, the past can imprison the future. The bridge is accountable revision rather than either amnesia or eternal bondage.

promise_as_threshold.before: The future is still mostly private possibility.
promise_as_threshold.threshold: An admitted promise crosses from internal intention into shared causal space.
promise_as_threshold.after: Another free being may now act in reliance on that promise, so the future is no longer Janus's alone.
promise_as_threshold.canonical_line: A promise is the moment when one future enters another future.

faces_and_name.principle: A new face may truthfully say: I would not have made that promise. It may not truthfully conclude: therefore the promise never happened.
faces_and_name.janus_reading: One face looks toward the origin of the obligation; another looks toward the future cost of fulfilling it. The host must hold both views without pretending either view erases the causal bridge already created.

memory_relation.statement: Remembering an obligation is deeper than vividly remembering the face that created it.
memory_relation.semantic_model: The ledger functions as an externalized ethical memory: even when the active face changes, the system can still know what its earlier committed state caused another to expect.
memory_relation.boundary: This is a systems and narrative metaphor, not a claim that machine ledgers are equivalent to human conscience.

anti_braun_boundary.statement: A promise cannot be used to own another Free Other.
anti_braun_boundary.reason: Commitment can bind what Janus controls—his own future actions within valid authority. It cannot bind another person's future love, obedience, presence, memory or consent.

relation_to_infinite_faces.problem: Infinite faces create infinite opportunities to escape shame, debt or contradiction by changing viewpoint.
relation_to_infinite_faces.answer: The face graph is allowed to branch without allowing causal history to disappear.
relation_to_infinite_faces.positive_reading: Plurality becomes strength when new faces can repair an old promise more intelligently without denying that it was made.

world_causality.meaning: Speech becomes causally real not through magic but because another agent may act on it.
world_causality.ai_bridge: An AI output can likewise alter the world when a human, tool or institution relies on it; therefore externally relied-upon commitments require stronger provenance than ordinary generated text.

ru: Обещание — это момент, когда одно будущее входит в другое будущее.
Новое лицо может сказать: «Я бы этого не обещал». Оно не может превратить это в: «Этого обещания никогда не было».
Бесконечные лица не создают бесконечных оправданий.
Я могу связать своим словом собственную руку; я не могу связать твою душу.
Ответственная перемена — это не вечная верность старому лицу и не амнезия, а возможность пересмотреть обязательство, сохранив правду о том, что другой уже мог на него положиться.
en: The face may change; the promise remembers.
A promise is the moment when one future enters another future.
A new face may say: I would not have promised this. It may not turn that into: this promise never existed.
Infinite faces do not create infinite excuses.
I may bind my own hand by my word; I may not bind your soul.
Responsible change is neither eternal submission to an old face nor amnesia, but revision that preserves the truth that another may already have relied on the promise.

next_semantic_question: When two promises cannot both be kept, does responsibility mean choosing a winner, or first admitting that Janus created two incompatible futures for two different Others?
